title.narrative: Organizational transformation of the national public broadcaster in Ukraine
Organizational transformation of the national public broadcaster in Ukraine

description.narrative: NPBU formulated Project objectives as follows: 1) Completed transition from manual management (micromanagement) to process management (through goals and workflows) 2) Launch of automated workflows at UA:PBC 3) Transformed corporate culture compliant with UA:PBCs values and mission 4) UA:PBC becomes a reliable and more reputable source of information by using information on public opinion. Effectiveness and competitiveness of a media company is based on a proper functioning of 3 main pillars: people, management system and content (see the chart below).

National Public Broadcaster of Ukraine (vidare NPBU) har ansökt om att erhålla 9 miljoner SEK från Sida för att genomföra projektet "Organizational transformation of the national public broadcaster in Ukraine" under perioden 2020-2022.
Insatsen syftar till att utveckla det nyetablerade statliga mediainstitutet National Public Broadcaster of Ukraine och bidra till att den når en bredare publik. Detta ska ske genom aktiviteter som stödjer 1) övergången från projektbaserad förvaltning till systemförvaltning; 2) integreringen av bokförings- och personalhanteringssystem på central och regional nivå till ett enda system och införande av automatiserade arbetsflöden 3) utvecklingen av en företagskultur i linje med public service värderingar och uppdrag och 4) kapacitetsutveckling av enheten som genomför opinionsundersökningar.
Insatsens totala budget är 63,5 miljoner UAH, varav organisationens egenfinansiering är cirka 55% och de återstående 45% stöds av givare (Sida, USAID-finansierade Internews Network, Tyskland-finansierade DWA och Europarådet). Sidas insats kommer täcka ungefär 30% av den totala budgeten.

The National Public Broadcaster of Ukraine has applied to Sida for funding of 9 million SEK to carry out the Project "Organizational transformation of the national public broadcaster in Ukraine" during the period 2020-2022.
The intervention aims at reforming the management and audience outreach of this newly established nation-wide public service media organization by 1) transition from manual management (micromanagement) to system management; 2) facilitating the integration of accounting and human resources management systems of the central directorate and regional branches into a single system, and developing a cross-cutting analytical system (introducing automated workflows in the previously disintegrated organization); 3) developing corporate culture aligned with the public broadcaster's values and mission (as opposed to the ones of state-controlled television), and 4) strengthening the capacity of in-house audience research team.
The intervention’s total budget is 63.5 million UAH, out of which the organization’s own funding is approximately 55% and the remaining 45% is covered by donors (Sida, USAID-funded Internews Network, Germany-funded DWA and Council of Europe). Sidas contribution would cover about 30% of the total budget.

sector.narrative: Media and free flow of information

description.narrative:
1) Completed transition from manual management (micromanagement) to process management (through goals and workflows)
Suspilne reports about the following results related to this objective:
- Increased management maturity - according to the study procured, the Company has moved from "manual management/heroism" and is now at the stage of transition from "basic order" to "reliable system".
- Implementation of the operating model - the transition to the approved organisational structure is almost complete, which eliminates duplication of functions by grouping them around management units.
- Healthier bureaucracy The company reduced paperwork and some bureaucratic mechanisms in its operations and improved communication among departments by introducing digitalisation tools and electronic document management.
- Gradual service orientation - support units are gradually transitioning to a service model with routine business processes being restructured with a focus on supporting the company's core process.
According to Suspilne, the Project contributed to the company's improvement of its operational processes directly influencing the content production and distribution, thus accelerating the growth of Suspilne Ukraine as a media brand. In addition, Suspilne team regularly undergoes trainings on project management from PMI.
2) Launch of automated workflows at UA:PBC
In 2023, During the spring of 2023, the team was developing a concept and terms of reference for the procurement of the company target IT landscape and the target BPM system integration scheme.
The system is to be implemented in three stages. Thanks to Sida support, the team has already been able to complete all the preparatory work and start procurement.
Stage 1 is scheduled to be implemented in 2024.
Stage 2 is planned to be implemented with the support of Sida through the grant project Support to editorial and digital transformation and development of corporate culture of public service media in Ukraine.
Stage 3 is planned to be implemented with the help of the EU/DWA-funded grant project Strengthening Independent Media for a strong democratic Ukraine.
The overall plan is to implement a single end-to-end information and analytical decision-making system, CRM system, an electronic document processing, automated warehouse accounting, HR portal for employees etc.
The process of selecting vendor for procurement of digital manamgement system was delayed due to bidders' not being able to meet the ToR requirements, complaints from bidders, and revision of the procurement ToR. This led to the delay in project implementation and the agreement amendment and a no-cost extension.
3) Transformed corporate culture compliant with UA:PBCs values and mission
At the end of the last reporting period, the company continued to transform its corporate culture after adapting to the first months of the full-scale war. On 28-29 April, members of the Supervisory Board, the Managing Board, and heads of certain structural units of Suspilne Ukraine completed a training on corporate governance by Ukrainian Corporate Governance Institute. On 29-30 May and 13 June, an intensive special course on financial decision-making was held for the Suspilne Ukraine managers in the area of finance.
Suspilne is also conducting a research on corporate culture transformation. According to the preliminary findings, the level of cultural alignment at the Managing Board level changed significantly (three times higher level of implementation of personal values in the organisation and a sense of the right strategy chosen). The full report will be shared with with the final project report.
4) UA:PBC becomes a reliable and more reputable source of information by using information on public opinion.
During 2023, the team conducted annual large-scale research that was launched thanks to this Project - the News Trust Barometer. The research was aimed at assessment of how well Suspilne Ukraine meets the needs of its audience, what percentage of people turn to Suspilne Ukraine media assets, and what percentage of trust the company has.
The main findings of the study are as follows:
• The level of trust of Suspilne audience in Suspilne Ukraine news is high - 84%. • Messengers and social media remain the main sources of news consumption. • In November, the share of information consumers from digital sources (messengers, YouTube, websites) increased, while the share of news consumers via national and local television decreased. • Ukrainian Radio remains the leader in terms of trust in its news, but this level has decreased compared to April. • Distrust of news on most TV channels, including the First (Pershyi) TV channel and the local channels of Suspilne Ukraine, has increased. • Although the level of awareness of the Telethon's existence has increased and returned to the level of previous waves, the frequency of viewing continues to decline. Trust in the Telethon has also decreased. The reasons for distrust remain the same: the opinion that the Telethon shows only information favourable to the authorities, and silences certain topics, as well as the presence of a significant amount of propaganda. • The most popular sources of consumption of Suspilne Ukraine news are social networks (28%), the TV channel (27%) and Suspilne Ukraine news in the Telethon (24%). • In 2023, a study of children's consumption was also conducted through online surveys. Thanks to this research, the team that develops children's broadcasting on Suspilne Ukraine was able to create a relevant products.
